copies.headline: Isaac's Questionable Tags Meet The League's Best Roster
copies.body:
The top-line gaps are small — Adam's plus-four at quarterback, plus-three at the top two backs, plus-four across three receivers, even at tight end — but that's the healthy version of Isaac's team, and Isaac doesn't have the healthy version. Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley, Jakobi Meyers, Dalton Kincaid and Cam Skattebo are all carrying tags. Lose Chase against Tennessee, with Cincinnati laying 10 in a 46.5-point game, and Isaac is starting Ryan Flournoy and Kalif Raymond, which is how you end up at 79 again. Behind Barkley there's J.K. Dobbins at six. The depth isn't there to absorb one scratch, let alone three.
Adam's floor is the whole argument. Jayden Daniels gets Philadelphia in a 40.5-total game where Washington is favored, Jaxon Smith-Njigba gets Chicago, and Kenneth Walker and Bucky Irving both sit in competitive spreads where neither team runs out the clock early. At 144.0 a game and 62-15 all-play, Adam has been the best team in the league by a comfortable distance. Isaac is 11th in scoring with +0.7 luck wins — he's 3-4 and has arguably outkicked that.

copies.headline: Logan Scores Enough, Loses Anyway, Again
copies.body:
Logan has the better quarterback and arguably the better backfield, and it still doesn't matter much. Burrow against a Titans team getting ten is the single best spot on either roster, and Jaylen Warren in a 39.5-total grinder against Cleveland is exactly the kind of ugly-but-fine 16 you need. The problem is everything after that. Jeremiyah Love, Zach Charbonnet and Braelon Allen are all questionable, so RB2 is a coin flip, and tight end is Colby Parkinson at 9 with Isaiah Likely at zero behind him. That's two lineup spots Logan can't fix from the bench.
Grant's edge is receiver depth in loud games. Zay Flowers in a 54.5 Baltimore-Buffalo track meet, with the Ravens underdogs and throwing late, is the highest-ceiling piece in this matchup. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable but Christian Watson at 14 covers it, and Goedert or Strange both clear Parkinson. Grant's 48% all-play says he's been lucky; this week he doesn't need to be.

copies.headline: Christian Is Too Good To Be 2-5
copies.body:
Christian is 2-5 with the third-best scoring average in the league and an all-play mark of 46-31, which is the statistical definition of getting mugged weekly. The edges here are small but they all point one way. Trevor Lawrence gets Indianapolis in a game Jacksonville is favored by 10, worth five over Michael Penix Jr., whose Falcons are catching 2.5 in Tampa. CeeDee Lamb headlines the best receiver room in this game in a 54.5-point total against Arizona, the highest number on the board. Running back is a dead heat at 31 apiece, so this comes down to quarterback and the top of the wideout group.
CJ's problem is the shape of the roster. Parker Washington at 16 leading your receivers is a projection, not a plan, and Emeka Egbuka and Rashee Rice both carry questionable tags. Behind Penix there's Tyler Shough at zero, and Ka'imi Fairbairn's kicker slot is a hole. CJ has banked half a win of luck already and sits ninth in the power rankings; Christian's floor over the last three weeks is 103, which still beats CJ's 90.9 from last Sunday.

copies.headline: Leif's Receiver Room Is a Waiting Room
copies.body:
Leif's path is Josh Allen and Derrick Henry in a 54.5-total game in Buffalo, which is a real path — Allen's 24 projection is the single biggest number on either roster, and Baltimore as a field-goal dog keeps that one honest into the fourth. The problem is everything behind them. Davante Adams is on IR, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey and David Montgomery all carry question marks, and Marvin Harrison Jr. projects at zero. That leaves Stefon Diggs in a 40.5-total slog against Philadelphia, Omar Cooper Jr. and Chris Godwin as the top three wideouts: 32 points of projection against Kaleb's 41, with nothing on the bench if someone lays an egg.
Kaleb wins this on volume of functional bodies. Drake London, Tre Tucker, Jordan Addison, KC Concepcion, Keenan Allen — even with Ladd McConkey and Carnell Tate questionable, he can field three double-digit receivers without flinching. Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall in the same 45.5-total Jets-Raiders game gives him 32 at running back. Goff gives back eight to Allen, and Kaleb's 109.2 per game says the ceiling is modest, but Leif needs Allen to go nuclear just to cover the gaps.

copies.headline: Two 1-6 Teams, One Unavoidable Winner
copies.body:
The positional math is close on paper and misleading underneath it. Mitchell's top-two backs project 37 to Noah's 32, but that's entirely Jahmyr Gibbs at 25 and he's questionable; behind him sit Rachaad White against a Philadelphia defense in a 40.5-total game and Jordan Mason in a Detroit-Minnesota matchup that favors the other side. The receiver room is worse than the 38 suggests — Nico Collins and Christian Kirk are projecting zero, and Matthew Golden and DJ Moore both carry tags. That's three or four question marks in one lineup. Noah's edge is simply that his pieces play.
Drake Maye is the biggest single advantage, a seven-point favorite in Miami with Rhamondre Stevenson and Hunter Henry stacked behind him, and Noah has actual replacement bodies — Michael Wilson, Josh Downs, Kendrick Bourne — if Jaylen Waddle sits. Mitchell's ceiling runs through Dak Prescott in a 54.5-total game against Arizona, and that's a real path. But two of his last three weeks were 85.5 and 79.4, and a roster this tagged doesn't stabilize on hope.

copies.headline: Peter's 5-2 Record Finally Meets Its Audit
copies.body:
The positional sheet says Peter wins three of four spots, but those edges are two and three points wide and all of them come with a QUESTIONABLE tag stapled on. Lamar Jackson in Buffalo with a 54.5 total is the best single game on either roster, except Peter's QB2 is Justin Herbert and the drop-off is eleven. A.J. Brown and George Pickens are both dinged; Pickens at least lands in Dallas-Arizona, the other 54.5 and the likeliest shootout on the slate. Brown's game is a 43.5 total where New England is favored by a touchdown and will happily run clock. The tight end gap is the only clean one, and it's John's: Trey McBride plus Brock Bowers versus Tucker Kraft and Mark Andrews.
John's floor is the real separator. Kyren Williams, Blake Corum and Puka Nacua all sit in a game the Rams are favored by 6.5 in, and the all-play numbers are brutal context — 65% for John, 43% for Peter, who has won two more games than he's earned. Peter scored 69.8 and 95.4 in two of the last three weeks. John hasn't dipped below 100 since September.

intro: The tightest game on the board is Leif at Kaleb, where Kaleb holds a slim edge and the loser drops out of the 5-2 tier that's currently chasing Adam — a one-game swing that reshuffles the top four. On the other end, Christian at CJ is the week's clearest gap despite the records, with Christian favored over a CJ roster that's been leaking production at the skill spots and can't afford a loss to a 2-5 team if it wants to stay in the bye hunt. Elsewhere, Mitchell at Noah is a 1-6 against a 1-6, which is less a matchup than a coin flip nobody asked to watch.
